correctness.rationale: The horizontal-strip quotient has the asserted intrinsic graph metric. For \(r\ge2\) the infinite-strip Rips complex is a directed union of finite dominated-column collapsible complexes and is contractible. Distinct deck translates lie farther than \(2r\), so edges lift uniquely. Every putative nonzero-winding triangle would, at equality \(n=3r\), force three full-horizontal-length edges with no layer switches, contradicting the row-flipping deck action. Flagness then gives unique higher-simplex lifts and a contractible \(\mathbb Z\)-cover. The resulting \(K(\mathbb Z,1)\) is a circle; commuting cover inclusions give stable \(\pi_1/H_1\) isomorphisms and an explicit scale-one graph loop generates the target \(H_1\). Standard-library exhaustive metric/lift/face checks pass in twelve stable cases; binary boundary ranks separately certify two lower-bound examples.
